original_narrative: During tripping out operation at Drilling Site DS-22 near Duliajan, Assam, a 5-inch drill pipe stand was being racked back in the derrick. The floorman was guiding the bottom of the drill pipe stand into the fingerboard when the air winch line slipped from the cathead. The suspended pipe stand swung violently across the rig floor (Line of Fire), pinning the floorman against the drawworks console. The floorman sustained severe crush injuries to the thorax and was declared deceased upon arrival at OIL Hospital, Duliajan. Investigation revealed that the air hoist wire rope was worn beyond discard criteria (3 broken strands in one lay length) and the winch operator did not have a clear line of sight to the floorman.

original_narrative: While picking up 9-5/8 inch casing joint from catwalk to drill floor via V-door at Well Pad WP-09, Moran oilfield, the single-joint pickup elevator latch opened unexpectedly midway up the ramp. The casing joint (weight approx. 1,400 kg) slipped out and slid down the V-door ramp at high velocity, crashing into the catwalk tub. Two roustabouts who were preparing the next joint on the catwalk had cleared the drop zone moments earlier following a verbal warning from the tool pusher. No injuries occurred, but catastrophic crush potential was present. The safety latch spring of the pickup elevator was found fatigued and jammed with dried drilling mud.

equipment_involved: Blowout Preventer (BOP), Tubing Hanger, Christmas Tree
original_narrative: During workover operations at Baghjan Well #5 near Duliajan, Assam, to test new gas producing sand, the workover crew pulled out the tubing string without properly killing the well or maintaining required hydrostatic overbalance. The Blowout Preventer (BOP) stack was not locked and hydraulic closing lines were disconnected during rig down without setting a mechanical barrier / back-pressure valve in the tubing hanger. A sudden gas kick occurred, leading to an uncontrolled blowout of natural gas and condensate at high pressure (approx. 4,200 psi), followed by fire after 14 days of uncontrolled release. Multiple emergency response barriers failed simultaneously.

original_narrative: At Drilling Site DS-41, Kumchai block, Arunachal Pradesh, maintenance crew was replacing the worn liner and piston of Triplex Mud Pump #2. While aligning the liner puller tool, the helper placed his left hand inside the fluid end module cavity. The hydraulic jack slipped off the crosshead extension rod due to oily surface, and the liner pulled back suddenly under residual spring tension, pinching the helper's left hand between the liner flange and pump housing. The helper suffered traumatic amputation of the left index and middle fingertips. The electrical drive motor had been locked out (LOTO), but hydraulic/mechanical residual energy was not isolated.

original_narrative: During preparatory grinding for a 14-inch crude oil pipeline branch connection near Jorhat Pump Station, contract welders were grinding the pipe surface to prepare the split-tee saddle area. The cold work permit was converted to hot work without conducting a formal gas test at the bottom of the bell-hole excavation. Grinding sparks landed on a pocket of trapped hydrocarbon vapor from a pinhole weeping leak at a nearby drain valve, causing a sudden flash fire in the trench. Two welders inside the 2-meter deep excavation suffered 2nd and 3rd degree burns to face and arms before scrambling out. No fire watch had been stationed at the edge of the pit with an extinguisher.

original_narrative: At Moran Crude Dispatch Terminal, pipeline technician was instructed to open the quick-opening closure (QOC) door on the 16-inch crude pig receiver following an intelligent pigging run. The technician checked the local pressure gauge which indicated 0 kg/cm² (gauge needle was stuck due to paraffin wax blockage). The technician loosened the safety interlock bolt and began unscrewing the central clamp. A sudden hiss and spray of trapped crude and nitrogen at 4.5 bar blew past the door seal, blasting the technician's safety goggles and helmet off. The technician was knocked backwards onto the gravel bund but suffered only minor abrasions. Had the locking lugs cleared, the 120 kg door would have blown open with fatal force.

equipment_involved: 10,000 KL Crude Oil Storage Tank, Mechanical Ventilation Fan
original_narrative: During 10-year internal inspection of 10,000 KL Crude Storage Tank #14 at Duliajan Central Tank Farm, two inspection engineers entered through the bottom manhole under a valid Confined Space Entry Permit. Forced air ventilation had been running for 48 hours. After 30 minutes inside, the sludge pump on an adjacent live tank malfunctioned, causing a backflow of sour vapor through an interconnected bottom drain header that had been valve-isolated but not physically blinded (spectacle blind was in open position). Portable 4-gas detector alarmed for H2S at 45 ppm (exceeding ceiling limit of 10 ppm). Standby person at manhole activated the air horn and both engineers evacuated with emergency EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) sets within 90 seconds, experiencing eye irritation and nausea.

equipment_involved: Flare Stack Platform (Height 28 meters), Full Body Harness
original_narrative: During annual turnaround at Digboi Refinery, an instrument technician was climbing the caged vertical ladder of the main flare stack (28 meters height) to replace the pilot thermocouple sensor. While transitioning from the ladder cage to the intermediate landing platform at 18 meters, the technician unclipped his double lanyard from the ladder lifeline without hooking either snap hook to the platform anchorage point. A strong gust of wind caused the technician to lose balance. He fell backward but his harness lanyard caught on an adjacent 2-inch structural bracing rod, leaving him suspended in mid-air at 16 meters. Emergency rescue team deployed a cherry picker to rescue him after 25 minutes. Technician suffered suspension trauma and severe bruising.

equipment_involved: 3.3 kV Switchgear Panel, Main Incomer Breaker
original_narrative: At Tengakhat GGS-IV, contract electrical supervisor was investigating an intermittent tripping alarm on the 3.3 kV high-pressure water injection pump motor. Without obtaining an Electrical Isolation Certificate or de-energizing the main 3.3 kV busbar, the supervisor opened the rear cubicle door using a defeated interlock key to test voltage with a standard multimeter (rated only up to 1000V). A phase-to-ground flashover occurred, producing an arc flash and blast wave. The blast blew the supervisor backward 3 meters, igniting his non-FR cotton boiler suit. Shift in-charge smothered the flames with fire blanket. The supervisor sustained 40% deep partial-thickness burns across upper torso and face.

equipment_involved: 80-Ton Hydraulic Telescopic Crane, Rig Mast Section
original_narrative: During exploration rig mast erection at Jaisalmer desert site ER-01 in Rajasthan, an 80-ton mobile crane was lifting the 18-ton derrick mast lower section. Ambient temperature was 46°C with loose sand terrain. Crane outrigger steel pads were placed directly on compacted sand without hardwood timber matting or steel spreader plates. As the boom swung to 14 meters radius at 85% capacity, the ground beneath the front-left outrigger gave way into a subsurface uncompacted void. The crane tilted 25 degrees, and the boom struck the generator skid with a loud impact. The rigger and banksman evacuated the exclusion zone in time; crane operator sustained shoulder sprain during emergency cab exit.

equipment_involved: High Pressure Slug Catcher, Gas Ultrasonic Flowmeter
original_narrative: At Kakinada Gas Processing Plant, high-pressure natural gas (72 bar) from offshore well lines entered the slug catcher header. During flowline valve changeover, a control room operator bypassed the automated low-temperature shutdown interlock (ESD-102) due to recurrent nuisance alarms. Condensate carryover caused severe hydrate formation and localized cryogenic chilling (-35°C) on downstream carbon steel piping, resulting in brittle fatigue fracture of a 2-inch impulse tubing fitting. A high-pressure gas jet was released into the compressor bay. The fixed infrared optical gas detector detected 35% LEL and successfully triggered the deluge sprinkler and automated ESD blowdown, preventing an explosion. Three operators nearby evacuated without injury.
